thread:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-affinity change yesterday, we're seeing 95th pct tail spikes on prefill-heavy workflows. KV cache hit rate dropped in the canary. Perf profiles attached.

maria: ugh, saw that. can you paste the numbers? :thinking:

alex: Sure. Baseline: prefill hit 0.93 -> now 0.47. decode still fine. Tail latency from 48ms -> 132ms on p95 for small prompts.

sam: do we have kernel routing logs? maybe requests are landing on quant kernels with slower KV paths.

alex: here's perf snippet from the canary node:
```
# perf top
Samples: 2K of event 'cpu-clock'
 20.1%  runtime          <kernel_affinity_select+0x120>
 17.8%  runtime          kv_cache_lookup
 12.6%  quant_kernels    q_matmul
```

leo: that runtime select spike looks suspicious. are prefill and decode walking same queue? last refactor merged them.

anya: I think the merged queue causes long prefill batches to hold KV hot entries open, starving decode paths. propose: separate initgen (prefill) queue from gen (decode) and enforce handshake window <= 5ms.

maria: sounds good. also suggest token_budget targets: prefill_budget=768, decode_budget=64 for small prompt classes. that'll keep prefill batching bounded.

sam: can we try a quick patch: 1) tag prefill requests with cls=initgen, 2) route to separate queue with lower max_batch_size and higher handshake priority, 3) set kernel_affinity_hint to prefer kv_warm kernels.

alex: I'll push a branch and run bench/continuous-batcher with profile enabled. CI job: `ci-bot run bench/continuous-batcher --profile --tag initgen-split`

ci-bot: Job queued: bench/continuous-batcher (initgen-split). Logs: https://ci.internal/2451000000

leo: if that fixes it, we should add a regression test that simulates mixed prefill/decode burst and asserts p95 < 80ms.

anya: agreed. also add observability metric: `queue.handshake_wait_ms` per queue.

maria: plan LGTM. alex, let us know when canary is up so we can validate tail.

alex: will report back in ~30m with results. :thumbsup:
